name: Exact iPhone and iPad model
plain: iOS Safari hides the exact device model.
meaning: The UA says only iPhone or iPad with a frozen OS string. Proxies: screen size (390x844 etc.) and DPR narrow to a generation, and WebGL renderer says Apple GPU. Exact model such as iPhone 15 vs 16 is often ambiguous, about 2 to 3 bits.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: screen width x height, dpr
fields.range: pins a size class (e.g. 390x844 at 3x is iPhone 12 to 16)

limits.headline: Can't see which exact iPhone or iPad you have
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: See that it is an iPhone or iPad
Guess a generation from screen size and pixel density
See a generic Apple GPU name
Tell Safari on iPhone from Chrome on Android
cannot: See the exact model, like iPhone 15 versus 16
See your iOS version in detail; it is frozen in the text
Get a clean answer; some models look the same
See your serial number or phone ID

story.what_it_is: iPhone Safari hides the exact iPhone or iPad model from sites.
story.for_you: A site knows you are on an iPhone, but not whether it is an older or a new one. It can still guess from your screen size, which narrows it down a lot.
story.for_makers: Apple freezes the details so all iPhones look alike. Developers must use screen size and graphics hints, which still narrow it to a generation. That keeps tracking weaker but not zero.

use_cases.example: A browser game wanted the exact iPhone model for settings and uses screen size and a quick benchmark.
A support team wanted the model for bug reports and asks the user or logs screen size.
An advertiser wanted to target iPhone Pro owners and guesses from screen size.
An accessory shop wanted the model to show the right case and asks you to choose.
A fraud tool wanted the true model and compares screen and graphics hints.
A streaming site wanted the model to pick HDR and uses media capability checks.
A product team wanted model counts and uses screen sizes as a stand in.

risks: Screen size still narrows it down

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
